prompts.prompt: Create one original educational biology illustration, friendly abstract comic style, rounded forms with clear thick drawn outlines, light mint/cream background, warm colors and generous spacing. Raster PNG, native landscape approximately1600×900,16:9. Main structures and the few large German labels must be readable at360px image width and680px. No photographic evidence, no title, no logo, no decorative fine print. The picture supports explanation; it is not a real learner experiment or performance. Show a simplified eukaryotic cell cycle in three spacious top panels, connected by single-headed clockwise progress arrows: INTERPHASE, MITOSE, ZELLTEILUNG. Use exact mixed-case labels Interphase, Mitose, Zellteilung. In Interphase show one intact cell with a nucleus; inside abstract blue DNA threads visibly duplicate from one complete information set to two copies, while the cell grows. Mitosis shows both equal complete copies partitioned into two daughter nuclei within one cell about to separate. Zellteilung shows two clearly separate daughter cells, one nucleus each and the same complete inherited information set. An outer arrow from one daughter back to Interphase closes the cycle. No meiotic chromosome reduction, no bacteria, no X chromosomes in interphase, no intricate DNA helix or microtext. In a separate bottom strip three big application icons with exact labels Wachstum, Reparatur, Vermehrung: growing multicellular plant; skin/tissue patch restoring a small wound; rooted multicellular plant cutting. No direct arrow claiming that a single division makes a whole plant. Keep ordered cycle transitions, nuclei, and equal daughter information biologically consistent. No additional labels.

Create one original educational biology illustration, friendly abstract comic style, rounded forms with clear thick drawn outlines, light mint/cream background, warm colors and generous spacing. Raster PNG, native landscape approximately1600×900,16:9. Main structures and the few large German labels must be readable at360px image width and680px. No photographic evidence, no title, no logo, no decorative fine print. The picture supports explanation; it is not a real learner experiment or performance. Show a conceptual mechanism of evolution in a population; use three large, spacious ordered stages, not a number-counting experiment. Top-left two separate simple origin boxes with large labels Mutation and Rekombination: Mutation changes just one blue genetic-information token to a new orange token; Rekombination combines already-existing parental blue and yellow tokens into a new combination, creating no new token type. Directed arrows from both origin boxes lead to a large middle-left group of equal-shaped light and dark beetles labelled Erbliche Variation. Then a large central dark-tree-bark scene labelled Selektion: a bird preferentially takes a more visible light beetle while multiple light and dark beetles still survive. A single clear arrow leads to a separate right group labelled Neue Generation, with a visibly higher proportion of dark beetles but still some light ones. Never recolour an individual, never show a light beetle turning dark, no organism climbing to a higher species or purposeful needs-driven mutations. Genetic origin boxes stay separate from the bird/selection scene; no arrow from predator to mutation. No precise counts, no percentages, no invented experimental data and no tiny text. All stage labels and the different population proportions must stay clear at360px. Use only exact labels Mutation, Rekombination, Erbliche Variation, Selektion, Neue Generation.
